geometry.derivationNote: The signed archival original and official PSZRI printing source-verify the legal inclusion of Crimea, Taman and the Kuban side on 19 April 1783. The independently pinned 1783–1787 full-state reconstruction has already passed distributed period controls and is the same geometry used by the verified post-Crimea base state. Replaying the change as a full-state replacement therefore materializes the legal acquisition without substituting modern administrative polygons or inferring a synthetic delta.

territoryChanges.notes: Geometry-verified on the russian-legal-border track by the already accepted post-Crimea 1783–1787 full-state fragment. International recognition and protectorate/claim layers remain separate.

geometry.derivationNote: The official bilingual treaty printing source-verifies recognition of Russian supreme authority and protection while preserving Kartli-Kakheti as a separate kingdom. This is therefore political-status metadata on the claim/sphere-of-control track, not a sovereign-territory mutation: it must not add Kartli-Kakheti to the Russian core-territory replay or require a Russian territory-area polygon. Any optional visualization of the protected kingdom belongs to a separate claim/dependency layer and must use period geometry independently of core territorial materialization.

routeSemantics.note: The later Treaty of Jassy explicitly confirms the 28 December 1783 act as concerning Crimea/Taman accession and the Kuban as the boundary in that sector.

geometry.derivationNote: The official federal archival chronology states that the act marked Ottoman recognition of Crimea's accession to Russia and established new borders. This is a recognition/status layer over the 1783 Russian acquisition rather than a second acquisition. Exact river/coastal geometry remains a separate period-geometry task.
